title: Good Scores, Bad Data: A Metric for Multimodal Coherence
abstract: arXiv:2603.25924v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Multimodal AI systems are evaluated by downstream task accuracy, but high accuracy does not mean the underlying data is coherent. A model can score well on Visual Question Answering (VQA) while its inputs contradict each other. We introduce the Multimodal Coherence Score (MCS), a metric that evaluates fusion quality independent of any downstream model. MCS decomposes coherence into four dimensions, identity, spatial, semantic, and decision, with weights learned via Nelder-Mead optimization. We evaluate on 1,000 Visual Genome images using DETR, CLIP, and ViLT, and validate on 150 COCO images with no retraining. Across three fusion architectures, MCS discriminates quality with higher sensitivity than task accuracy alone (Spearman rho = 0.093 vs. 0.071). Perturbation experiments confirm each dimension responds independently to its failure mode with zero cross-talk. MCS is lightweight, requires no human annotation, and tells you no

translated_title: 好分数，坏数据：一种多模态一致性度量
translated_abstract: 多模态AI系统通常通过下游任务准确率来评估，但高准确率并不意味着底层数据是一致的。一个模型可以在视觉问答（VQA）上取得高分，而其输入却相互矛盾。我们提出了多模态一致性得分（MCS），这是一种独立于任何下游模型来评估融合质量的度量指标。MCS将一致性分解为四个维度：身份、空间、语义和决策，其权重通过Nelder-Mead优化方法学习得到。我们在1,000张Visual Genome图像上使用DETR、CLIP和ViLT进行评估，并在150张COCO图像上无需重新训练进行验证。在三种融合架构中，MCS区分数据质量的灵敏度高于仅使用任务准确率（Spearman rho = 0.093 vs. 0.071）。扰动实验证实每个维度独立响应其对应的失效模式，且无交叉干扰。MCS轻量级、无需人工标注，并且能够告诉你……
tldr: 提出多模态一致性得分（MCS），一种轻量级、无需人工标注的指标，通过将一致性分解为身份、空间、语义、决策四个维度来独立于下游模型评估多模态融合质量，其区分质量的灵敏度高于任务准确率。
en_tdlr: Proposes the Multimodal Coherence Score (MCS), a lightweight, annotation-free metric that evaluates multimodal fusion quality independently of downstream models by decomposing coherence into identity, spatial, semantic, and decision dimensions, achieving higher sensitivity than task accuracy alone.
